title: Amazon SDE2 interview experience (offer)
text:
# Amazon SDE2 interview experience

I interviewed for SDE2 at Amazon in Seattle last month and got the offer.

## Online assessment
Two problems in 90 minutes. The first was to find the number of islands in a grid of 0s and 1s. The second asked for the minimum cost to connect all ropes, which I solved with a min-heap.

## Onsite
Round 1 (coding): implement an LRU cache with O(1) get and put. The interviewer then asked how I would make it thread-safe.

Round 2 (system design): design a URL shortener that handles 100 million new links a day. We talked about base62 keys, the key-value store, and caching hot links.

Round 3 (behavioral, bar raiser): tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager. Also: describe a time you delivered under a tight deadline.

Overall the bar raiser focused heavily on leadership principles. Prepare STAR stories.

title: Understanding the Saga pattern
text:
# Understanding the Saga pattern

In a microservice architecture a business transaction often spans several services, each with its own database. Two-phase commit is rarely an option, so the Saga pattern breaks the transaction into a sequence of local transactions. Each step publishes an event that triggers the next one; if a step fails, compensating transactions undo the work of the steps before it.

There are two ways to coordinate a saga. In choreography, services react to each other's events without a central coordinator. In orchestration, an orchestrator tells each service what to do next.

Choreography is simple for short flows but gets hard to follow; orchestration keeps the flow in one place at the cost of another component. This pattern also shows up in system design interviews, so it is worth knowing.

Next week: the outbox pattern and exactly-once publishing.

title: 字节跳动后端一面二面面经
text:
# 字节跳动后端面经

上周面了字节跳动的后端开发岗位，记录一下。

一面（技术）：先聊项目，然后问了 TCP 三次握手为什么不是两次，接着问了 MySQL 的索引为什么用 B+ 树。算法题是反转链表的第 m 到第 n 个节点。

二面（技术）：问了 Redis 的持久化方式（RDB 和 AOF）各有什么优缺点，又问了如何设计一个秒杀系统、如何防止超卖。最后写了一道题：求数组中第 K 大的元素。

整体感觉问得很细，项目要准备好。

title: Google L4 onsite, rejected but learned a lot
text:
# Google L4 onsite

Phone screen: given a string, return the first non-repeating character. Easy, then the follow-up was to do it for a stream of characters.

Onsite coding 1: merge overlapping intervals, then insert a new interval into a sorted list of intervals.

Onsite coding 2: word ladder: the shortest transformation sequence from one word to another, changing one letter at a time. BFS.

Onsite coding 3: design a data structure that supports insert, delete and getRandom in O(1).

Googleyness: how would you handle a teammate who keeps missing code review deadlines?

I was rejected on coding 3: I used a hash map but forgot to swap with the last element when deleting.

title: Why I stopped grinding LeetCode
text:
# Why I stopped grinding LeetCode

For two years I solved a problem every morning before work. I had a spreadsheet, a streak, and a lot of anxiety. Last spring I stopped, and my career did not fall apart.

What changed was where I spent the time: reading code from projects I admired, writing design notes for my team, and pairing with juniors. My next job search took longer to prepare for but the conversations were better.

Is grinding useless? No. But it is one tool. If you are early in your career, a few months of practice helps. After that, the marginal problem teaches little. What matters more is being able to explain trade-offs and to write code people want to maintain.

What do you think?

title: Stripe onsite: bug squash, integration and a ledger design
text:
# Stripe onsite

Stripe's loop is different from big tech.

Bug squash: I got a small Ruby codebase with failing tests and had to find and fix the bugs in 45 minutes. One bug was an off-by-one in pagination.

Integration round: call a mock HTTP API, handle pagination and retries with backoff, and aggregate the results into a report.

System design: design a double-entry ledger for payments. They asked how to make the API idempotent so a retried request does not charge twice.

Behavioral with the hiring manager: why Stripe, and tell me about a time you improved a process nobody owned.

title: Java 面试高频题整理
text:
# Java 面试高频题

整理了最近面试中被问到最多的 Java 题：

1. HashMap 的底层结构是什么？为什么链表长度超过 8 会转成红黑树？
2. synchronized 和 ReentrantLock 有什么区别？
3. volatile 关键字的作用是什么？能保证原子性吗？
4. JVM 的垃圾回收算法有哪些？G1 和 CMS 的区别？
5. 线程池的核心参数有哪些？任务队列满了会怎样？

希望对大家有帮助。

title: Month six of the job search
text:
# Month six of the job search

Six months, 240 applications, 11 recruiter calls, 3 onsites, 0 offers. I am tired. Every rejection email sounds the same and none of them say why.

I keep a spreadsheet so I can see progress even when there is none. I go for a walk every afternoon. I volunteered to help a local nonprofit with their website, which at least means I am writing code for someone.

If you are in the same place: you are not alone. Take breaks. The market is not a verdict on you.

I will post again when something changes.

title: Meta E5 interview loop
text:
# Meta E5 loop

Two coding rounds, one system design, one behavioral.

Coding 1: valid palindrome II (you may delete at most one character), then the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a binary tree.

Coding 2: given a list of accounts with emails, merge accounts that share an email. I used union-find. Second problem: the k closest points to the origin.

System design (product): design Instagram's news feed. Focus on fan-out, ranking and caching.

Behavioral: a time you had to push back on a product decision; a time you mentored someone.

title: Announcing our open-source load testing tool
text:
# Announcing Thrum 1.0

Today we are releasing Thrum, an open-source load testing tool written in Rust. It generates HTTP traffic from a YAML scenario, ramps users up and down, and reports p50, p95 and p99 latencies in real time.

Why another tool? Existing ones either needed a JVM or could not keep up above 50k requests per second on one machine. Thrum does 300k on a laptop.

Get started with `cargo install thrum`, write a scenario, and run `thrum run scenario.yaml`. We would love feedback and contributions. We are also hiring: if you like performance work, our interview is a take-home load test of a small service.

title: Uber SDE2 virtual onsite
text:
# Uber SDE2 virtual onsite

Recruiter call, then a 60-minute phone screen: design a hit counter that returns the number of hits in the last five minutes.

Onsite:
- Coding: find the median from a data stream (two heaps).
- Coding: course schedule: can all courses be finished given prerequisites? Then return an order.
- System design: design a ride matching service for drivers and riders, with surge pricing.
- Behavioral: tell me about the most complex project you worked on.

I got an offer at L4 instead of L5.

title: 腾讯 WXG 后台开发实习面经
text:
# 腾讯 WXG 后台实习面经

一面：自我介绍之后，问了进程和线程的区别、进程间通信有哪些方式。然后问 epoll 和 select 的区别。手撕代码：用两个栈实现一个队列。

二面：主要聊项目，问了如果数据库主从延迟导致读到旧数据怎么处理，以及一致性哈希是怎么回事。最后一道算法：最长递增子序列。

三面 HR：为什么选择腾讯，以及职业规划。
